title: A test run says what is wrong with the code, not with the build folder
goal: When somebody adds a field to a core type, the test command can report twenty tests broken and crash the runner, on code that is perfectly fine: the build folder keeps half-rebuilt pieces that disagree about the shape of the type. Make the test command notice that and rebuild rather than reporting a failure nobody can explain.
notes: REPRODUCED 2026-09-20 while building ClipPieces. Added one optional stored property (Layer.cuts) to Sources/PhotonzCore/Layer.swift, then `Scripts/test.sh`: 20 failures in Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/SeparatedRowsSayTheirWordsTests.swift plus `exited with unexpected signal code 11`. Every failure was the same shape - every run of text read as empty, so rows kept their numbered names: `(names -> ["Text 9", ... "Background"]).contains(words -> "General")`. The crash report (node Scripts/crash-report.mjs --file ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/swiftpm-testing-helper-2026-09-20-054858.ips) is EXC_BAD_ACCESS KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x8 in swift_retain < outlined init with copy of Layer < openingASavedReadingLeavesNothingPending(). That is PhotonzRenderTests reading a Layer at the OLD field offsets: isARunOfText comes back false for every piece so nothing is read, and a copy retains whatever is at the wrong offset. PROVED it was the build folder and not the code, three runs: (1) with the change, `Scripts/test.sh --filter SeparatedRowsSayTheirWords` = 20 failures + signal 11; (2) same filter with the three files moved out of the tree = 11 tests passed; (3) `rm -rf .build` then the same filter with the change back in = 11 tests passed, and the full suite then passed 8509 tests in 675 suites. So swiftpm did not rebuild PhotonzRenderTests against the new layout. Why it matters here rather than being a toolchain curiosity: this is the command every runner must have green before it commits, and it spent fifteen minutes of this task looking like a real memory bug in the app. The cheap answer is probably for Scripts/test.sh to notice a signal-11 exit and retry once from a clean .build, saying which it did.
acceptance: Adding a stored property to Layer and running Scripts/test.sh either passes or fails for a real reason, never with a crash inside a copy of a layer
A run that hits the stale case says so in words and rebuilds, rather than printing failures that look like broken code
The fix costs an ordinary run no noticeable time

log.note: READ the-test-suite-stops-reporting-failures-that-are BEFORE diagnosing. It watched the same eleven SeparatedRowsSayTheirWords tests go red with every text read empty, but from machine LOAD rather than a stale .build: idle passes, busy fails, same tree, no signal 11. So an empty text read is not proof of this task's stale-build case; the crash inside a copy of Layer is.

Hit again on 2026-09-21, exactly as this task describes. Adding two stored properties (key, matte) to LayerStyle and running Scripts/test.sh gave: "error: Process '.../swiftpm-testing-helper ...' exited with unexpected signal code 11". The crash report's faulting frames were 'outlined destroy of LayerStyle < BorderEffectRenderTests.filledBox(_:)' — a render test that never touches the new fields, failing because the test module was still compiled against the old layout. It reproduced three times running with --filter BorderEffectRenderTests, so it reads exactly like a deterministic bug in the app. rm -rf .build and a clean run gave 8807 passing. Cost about twelve minutes of a task's turn: the only way to tell it from a real regression was to stash the whole change and run the suite twice (192s each).
